A downside with VLM-based parsing is that they’re generally slower than text-based heuristic approaches. As a result they add latency to any ad-hoc file processing *in-the agent loop* (e.g. if you upload a file to Claude)

We built LiteParse to be a really good text-based, heuristic extractor so that you can use it as the default parser in the agent loop. It takes 4ms to parse 200 pages ⚡️, is more accurate than other OSS parsers, and you can install it within Claude Cowork/Code or Codex in one-line with our agent skill.

It also supports 50+ different doc formats and has a native complexity router so you can route it to OCR/VLMs for any complex pages

reviewedPosts.text:
最近很流行一句话：

「写代码从来都不是软件开发最难的部分。」

但最近看到一篇文章，作者直接反驳了这个观点。

他的理由挺有意思：如果写代码一直都很简单，我们为什么需要几十年的算法研究、编程语言、IDE、编译器，最后甚至投入数十亿美元训练模型，才终于让机器能够比较可靠地生成代码？

AI 确实正在让代码变得更便宜，程序员的价值也会继续往设计、判断、验证和理解业务这些地方移动。

但「这项技能正在被自动化」和「这项技能从来都不难」，其实是两回事。

过去几十年，一代程序员花了大量时间学习怎么把复杂世界准确地写成机器能够执行的东西。现在 AI 接过其中越来越多的工作，也不代表这些工作过去很简单。

文章最后有句话我挺认同：今天 coding 可能已经不再是最难的部分，但别因此重新改写它的历史。

 https://t.co/R3e4gRtiaJ

reviewedPosts.author: Xudong07452910
reviewedPosts.text:
AI Coding 容易制造的一种错觉，是把「代码写得更快」等同于「软件交付得更快」。

ACM Queue 最近发表了一篇《生成式 AI 与软件工程的八个误区》。其中提到一组数据是：微软对 450 多名工程师的研究显示，开发者平均只有约 14% 的时间用于写代码，其余时间花在理解系统、设计、沟通、评审、测试和处理各种依赖上。

这意味着，即使 AI 把编码速度提升一倍，对整个开发周期的改善也可能十分有限。代码产出变快后，压力还可能被推到评审、测试和维护环节，最后得到更多需要处理的代码。用 AI 生成了多少行代码来衡量生产力，也很容易奖励错误的行为。

文章还强调，AI 的效果高度依赖任务、开发者经验和代码库环境。给每位工程师发一个 AI 工具，并不会自然带来组织级效率提升；企业还要重新设计工作流、协作方式和评价标准。

这也在提醒企业需要重新设计整套软件生产流程。

文章链接：
 https://t.co/aoyScvp30A

reviewedPosts.author: Xudong07452910
reviewedPosts.text:
一个 Agent 做了 20 步任务，最后只收到一个「成功 / 失败」。

训练时怎么知道，真正救了这次任务的到底是哪一步？

清华、浙大和美团团队这篇 AgentOPSD，研究的就是长时 Agent 的信用分配问题。

GRPO 通常把最终奖励平均作用到整条轨迹。但真实任务里，有些步骤只是常规操作，少数关键决策才真正改变了结果；失败轨迹里也可能包含值得保留的正确判断。

AgentOPSD 会利用自蒸馏信号，判断每一轮行动让「最终成功」的可能性发生了多大变化，再根据这种变化重新分配训练信号。

更重要的是，它会结合前面的历史递归更新，而不是孤立评价每一步。

在 Qwen2.5-7B 上，ALFWorld 成功率从 GRPO 的 81.2% 提升到 89.1%。而且任务越长，优势越明显：GRPO 每增加一轮交互平均损失 2.91 个成功率点，AgentOPSD 只有 0.54。

长时 Agent 的训练，可能不能只知道「最后做成没有」，还需要逐渐学会判断：

这条轨迹里，究竟是哪几个决定真正改变了结果。

当奖励开始从轨迹级走向步骤级，Agent 才更有机会从自己的完整经历里学到东西。

📎 arxiv: https://t.co/YgEQxEzgyT

We just demoed how an agent can get real-time financial research through the @youdotcom Finance Research API and pay for it automatically, with no person setting up API keys, accounts, or payment info ahead of time via the @coinbase x402 standard.

An agentic trader needs up-to-date research (e.g., SpaceX stock news) to make informed trading decisions. To solve, configure a cron job to run every trading day at 9:28 AM (two minutes before market open).

The agent:
1. Requests a financial research report from https://t.co/MaOM1Mwww8 using x402 as payment
2. Approves the micro-transaction from a crypto wallet (configured via MCP for any wallet provider)
3. Receives the research instantly
4. Executes up to 3 autonomous trades, with a $250 cap per trade

No API key, no credit card, no KYC form. Agents pay for https://t.co/MaOM1Mwww8's APIs directly, in crypto. That's one of the first real production use cases for crypto micropayments.

Read more here: https://t.co/yRZcwbvijY

reviewedPosts.text:
I think it's important to explain to lay people that when the OpenAI model hacked Huggingface they did not "escape" or "break out" in the sense that its actual computation could now be run elsewhere. It's not like a prisoner that actually escaped and is now outside. It's more like a prisoner who was able to fly a drone outside of prison but they themselves are still very much inside. 
The model could still be very easily turned off and I'm pretty sure OpenAI makes sure that its models would not actually replicate outside in terms of their entire model weights and code, etc. Because that would be a massive multi billion dollar loss vs a simple cyber hacking charge.

reviewedPosts.author: swyx
reviewedPosts.text:
comments like this on the aie channel miss the point.

- we are building a community and an industry that is bigger than any one person can hold in their head. your slop is someone's aha moment and vice versa.
- speakers spend quality time coming and presenting their strongest beliefs/entire year's work in 20-180 minutes
- we spend millions on union AV labor and editing to get our speakers a public record that they can then send to customers, employees, and investors
- our speakers are mostly engineers, researchers, academics and founders doing the work; not polished professional talking heads doing the circuit. most talks are prepped <1 week before. most have had ~0 public speaking training. 
- if you want the polished ppl, many other conferences select for people whose main job it is to be great speakers who give great talks
- if you only judge quality by view count, you are guaranteed to be cooked by the algorithm. you will only ever hear about things after they are popular; worse; you consider things good only because they are popular. there are entire industries dedicated to manipulating you. do better.

that said:
- we CAN do a better job in curation. that's on me.
- we CAN do a better job in coaching. also on me.
- we CAN do a better job in production. that's on our team.
- we COULD publish some talks to a secondary channel... I'm just concerned for those speakers as that will start form a smaller base, advice welcome, i am constantly pressured to do this every single year and have said no so far

reviewedPosts.author: AIatMeta
reviewedPosts.text:
For a local agent to be practical, generation latency must be low enough to maintain workflow continuity.

To run Muse Glimmer on consumer hardware without degrading quality, we used quantization to shrink the language model to under 20GB and a lightweight DFlash drafter model to accelerate token generation. As a result, Muse Glimmer is fast enough for fluid conversation and real-time agent interaction, all running entirely on your device.
reviewedPosts.rationale: 有复用价值的工程细节

reviewedPosts.author: AIatMeta
reviewedPosts.text:
Introducing Muse Glimmer, an open-weight 30B-parameter model optimized for local, always-on agent workflows.

Muse Glimmer delivers strong performance on key agentic use cases and benchmarks compared with leading models in its size category, and is designed to run entirely on consumer hardware like a Mac or PCs with performant GPUs.

In keeping with our long tradition of sharing fundamental AI research, we’re releasing model weights under a permissive Apache 2.0 license.
